answers.Q1: Every composer in the set treats scheduling as a property of the send action, not a separate feature: Slack's send-button dropdown with presets and a custom date/time (mobbin:fd356e91), Whop's inline calendar popover (mobbin:16eb85ed), LinkedIn's clock icon (refero:863), Basecamp's 'Schedule and save' (mobbin:25c42c82). Audience targeting is rarer and coarser than the question assumes: Google Classroom puts a 'For / All students' dropdown directly above the text box (refero:19605564), Teachable offers everyone / a course / an individual (refero:9617), The Leap uses described segments (refero:4564), and Confluence only Public/Private plus a start–end window (mobbin:fcc604e7). Attachments are inline uploads (ClassDojo photo, Basecamp PDF, Whop image); nobody attaches from a course library. Only The Leap closes the loop from recipients through confirmation to open/click stats. Confluence's one-active-banner cap is the caveat: a persistent materials banner and a timely one cannot coexist.
answers.Q2: Two models. 'One composer, many channels' puts the channel as a control on the same post: beehiiv's Post / Email / Website / Delivery tabs reconcile into a per-channel recipient summary before sending (mobbin:748e794e); Kit layers a 'Publish to web' opt-in over a default email send (mobbin:f722d4bb); Intercom folds platform (web / iOS / Android) and push into one panel (mobbin:7380bc5c). 'Implicit channel' treats the in-app post as the channel and only asks who is notified: Basecamp separates 'who should see this' from 'when I post this, notify…' (mobbin:0bc24c79), and Substack bundles email and push into a single default-on 'notify subscribers' toggle (mobbin:a7ebc4ec). Nobody in the set exposes an external LMS as a channel inside the composer; that lives in an export menu (see Q5). The useful distinction for a course is visibility versus notification: the post is the record, the channels are how people hear about it.
answers.Q3: Link controls converge on one panel with five questions: who can open (anyone / workspace / specific people), at what level (view / comment / edit), until when, with which password, and how to revoke. Mural shows all five, including a timezone-stamped expiry and a 'Reset visitor link' that regenerates rather than merely disables (mobbin:836e980f); Proton has expiry, password and 'Stop sharing' (mobbin:ef4fcd7f); Notion resolves relative presets ('in a week') to an absolute date inline and ends with a red Remove (mobbin:cfca14fb). Coda (mobbin:c333ff8e), Dropbox (mobbin:777c4ef0) and Sketch (mobbin:1fb17c11) focus on tiered access (workspace / guests / everyone) and per-person levels, with Copy link always in the same corner; Sketch splits public rights into download versus comment checkboxes. Only Loom shows tracking next to the share ('No views yet', refero:1242). ClickUp is the counter-example (mobbin:7f248abd): expiry defaults to Never with no presets, no access level, and the only revoke is an all-or-nothing Unpublish.
answers.Q4: Feedback is worth having only when it is per person and has an action next to it. Navan lists each invitee with a status, lets you select the non-responders and 'Send a reminder' from the same table (mobbin:9d8af34f); Superhuman shows per-person, per-device, timestamped opens inline on the thread itself (mobbin:ba56c2de). Automation goes further: HoneyBook branches the follow-up on 'file viewed within 1 day' (mobbin:8afb0d65); Docusign lets you set the days before the first reminder and the repeat interval (mobbin:e4a526c1). Newsletter tools lead with aggregate counters (Mailchimp mobbin:6db18da5, HubSpot mobbin:5814d24c; Dub for link clicks, refero:2fe44823) and keep per-recipient detail one tab away (Outseta's Recipients tab with last-opened timestamps, mobbin:34451b74). WhatsApp's Delivered / Read is the minimum: two states, one recipient (mobbin:5580e66f). Square's Announcements list is the caution (mobbin:1c8c3422): a 'Seen by' column that shows nothing and offers no follow-up action.
answers.Q5: The thinnest question in the set and the most important one for Essentials. Only SchoolAI shows a complete hand-off (mobbin:3135010e): an Export menu that lists Google Classroom next to Docs / PDF, a permission modal that says what will be shared, an OAuth enable step, a Class picker that maps the document to one specific class, and an 'Exported to Google Classroom!' toast. Course platforms in the set have no hand-off at all: in Kajabi, publishing inside the product is the send, so the learner-facing surface is the product's own portal (mobbin:9aa981d2). Generic connectors stop at authorization: Craft is a Connect / Disconnect toggle on a settings page (mobbin:e9079303), and Cofounder's OAuth flow with per-scope toggles never reaches a 'what was sent' or success state (mobbin:7897406d, counter-example). Nobody shows editing or re-syncing after the hand-off.
answers.Q6: The consistent products give announcements a distinct type or place on the learner side. Microsoft Teams offers 'Post' versus 'Announcement' in the composer and renders announcements with a bold title and replies attached (mobbin:88ad5199); Circle routes them to an 'Announcements' space separate from the feed (mobbin:c1b1c3ad); ClassDojo keeps a teacher-only Pin so the post stays on top, with the attachment and replies inline (mobbin:3edf67a5). Unread state is aggregated centrally in Slack's Activity screen rather than only inside the source channel (mobbin:8e65f9c9), and Spotify lets the recipient choose email versus push per category, a model for learner notification preferences (refero:471b8f0c). Coursera is the counter-example (mobbin:36db9592): instructor content sits in a 'Latest'-sorted Q&A list with no pin, no unread marker and no sender role, so an announcement is indistinguishable from peer chatter.
